comments.body:
The misinterpretation is happening in Jena Prologue .-

The result is that the update statement returned by the parser is :

INSERT <http://localhost:8080/rest/object1> <http://myurl.orgpackage> "ppp" WHERE {}

versus:

INSERT <http://localhost:8080/rest/object1> <http://myurl.org/package> "ppp" WHERE {}

I think one way around this grammar issue would be updating the FedoraLdp code (in this case the patch method) to do a regex check/substitution for urls without a terminating slash.

Osman Din, since this issue would also be observed by someone using F4 in an embedded configuration (no REST-API), could your solution be pushed deeper into the stack? For example, in JcrPropertyStatementListener?

PR https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/739

Please note that there were minor updates to this PR.

Please merge the following PR into your branch if you agree:
https://github.com/osmandin/fcrepo4/pull/2

I added a comment related to the rollback:

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/739#issuecomment-77781019

Ok, the bug is coming from the following Jena method:

https://github.com/apache/jena/blob/f243e9e0eec72407f855be3b718f142380bda758/jena-core/src/main/java/com/hp/hpl/jena/rdf/model/impl/Util.java#L46

Basically, our kernel-impl PropertyConverter ends up relying on this method via:

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-impl/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/impl/rdf/converters/PropertyConverter.java#L116

L116 gets the namespace as "http://", instead of the full "http://myurl.org", and then of course Modeshape registers "http://" as ns001, etc.

So, the namespace map from Jena is correct (I checked). As a confirmation test, when I manipulate the PropertyConverter to substitute "http://" with "http://myurl.org", the IT correctly identifies the node property "esc:myurl.orgp" (mushed as per cbeer's spec reference).

However, when I print the Model, the triple seems to be:

[info:fedora/testRefObject, http://myurl.orgmyurl.orgp, "aaa"]

whereas, if I don't touch PropertyConverter, the triple is:

[info:fedora/testRefObject, http://myurl.orgp, "aaa"]

So, I'm not sure if reporting/patching the Jena Util.java method would not introduce some other kind of issue (while it seems to definitely address this current JIRA issue).

Please let me know what you think.

Can you be more specific about where the bug is being introduced in:
https://github.com/apache/jena/blob/f243e9e0eec72407f855be3b718f142380bda758/jena-core/src/main/java/com/hp/hpl/jena/rdf/model/impl/Util.java#L46

And what a patch would look like?

You say the namespace map from Jena is correct, but you also say there is a bug in Jena. So I am unclear as to where the issue actually is.

The issue is in this specific utility method we're indirectly relying on in PropertyConverter (and likely not with other namespace population logic, in whatever package or method or classes that resides in Jena).

The specific lines are 70-72. It looks for a terminating character (working backwards), and the first slash it can find backwards in “http://myurl.org” is “http://“. When PropertyConverter asks for a namespace to lookup/register in JCR, it gets "http://", and registers “http://“ (as opposed to getting "http://myurl.org").

Looking at the method’s Javadoc, it seems that the method is correct technically, but its usage is broken as far as PropetryConverter is concerned. Currently, I'm not familiar with their API or the source code to guess what a patch would look like if necessary. This method is called by other Jena methods as well.

This task is to determine where in the application stack sparql-update requests, like the one below, are having their namespace declaration mis-interpreted.
The following example should successfully create a "esc" namespace prefix.

  1. Request
    curl -i -XPATCH -H"Content-Type: application/sparql-update" --data-binary @props.sparql localhost:8080/rest/testcontainer
  1. Where, props.sparql is:
    ---------------
    PREFIX esc: <http://myurl.org>
    INSERT { <> esc:package "ppp"; }

    WHERE { }
    ---------------

See: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/fedora-tech/rk8U4KCKWbc/2J6bZkP3AxwJ
